cards.q: Where does OSPF summarize routes and what commands are used?
cards.a: OSPF summarizes routes only at the ABR using area X range for inter-area routes, and at the ASBR using summary-address for external (redistributed) routes. OSPF cannot summarize inside an area - LSAs are always exact within the area. Summarization shrinks the LSDB, reduces SPF, and contains flaps.

cards.q: What are the two commands that answer 'how do I summarize OSPF?'
cards.a: area X range at the ABR aggregates inter-area routes (Type 3), and summary-address at the ASBR aggregates external redistributed routes (Type 5/7). Summarization inside an area is not possible - intra-area must be exact.

cards.q: How do you use area X range on the ABR?
cards.a: Enter router ospf 1 and area 1 range 10.1.0.0 255.255.0.0 to aggregate area-1 internal routes into a single Type 3. The not-advertise option suppresses the aggregate as a filter, multiple ranges are allowed, and the most specific covering summary wins.

cards.q: How do you use summary-address on the ASBR?
cards.a: Enter router ospf 1 and summary-address 10.2.0.0 255.255.0.0 with redistribute static subnets to aggregate Type 5 external routes at the ASBR. It also applies to Type 7 (NSSA) external routes on the translating ABR.

cards.q: What are the benefits of OSPF summarization?
cards.a: Smaller LSDB (fewer Type 3/5 LSAs), less SPF CPU (shorter SPF run), stability (a flap inside the summarized range doesn't propagate), determinism (one aggregate at the boundary), and a smaller routing table in the RIB/FIB.

cards.q: What is the null0/discard concern with OSPF summarization?
cards.a: A router advertising an aggregate must discard traffic to sub-ranges it doesn't have, otherwise it could re-advertise or loop. The ABR/ASBR generating the summary also needs a matching path or a Null0 for the covered ranges. The discard-route option generates the discard on some platforms.
show ip ospf database summary shows the Type 3 summaries, show ip ospf database external shows the Type 5 view, and show ip route ospf shows resulting routes.

cards.q: What does the not-advertise option do in OSPF summarization?
cards.a: not-advertise suppresses the aggregate route, effectively using the range as a filter rather than advertising it.

cards.q: Can OSPF summarize routes inside an area?
cards.a: No. OSPF cannot summarize inside an area - intra-area LSAs are always exact. Summarization only happens at the ABR (inter-area, area X range) and ASBR (external, summary-address).
No. OSPF summarization is not auto-summarization - there is no classful auto behavior. You must explicitly configure area X range or summary-address at the boundary routers.

cards.q: Does OSPF summarization apply to Type 7 NSSA external routes?
cards.a: Yes. summary-address at the ASBR applies to Type 5 external routes and also to Type 7 (NSSA) external routes on the translating ABR.

cards.q: Summarize the OSPF summarization quick-review facts.
cards.a: Inter-area uses ABR area X range; external uses ASBR summary-address; inside an area is not possible; Type 3 target for inter-area summaries; Type 5/7 target for external; not-advertise suppresses the range; discard-route drops covered ranges; benefit is smaller LSDB and less SPF; flaps are contained at the boundary.
